title: Giving companies more control over their AI agents, with NVIDIA
summary: Claude Managed Agents offers composable APIs for production agents with layered security, credential management, and audit trails. Credentials are held in separate vaults inaccessible to agents; NVIDIA OpenShell integration enforces policies outside the model, enabling enterprises to formally verify agent access and set narrow permissions.

title: Coding sessions are longer and use more context. Claude Opus 5.5 is built with that in mind.
summary: Claude Opus 5.5 is optimized for long, context-heavy coding and costs 40% less to run than Opus 5. Cached token pricing dropped 60% with 50% fewer cache misses; output is 30% faster than its predecessor.

title: Claude Tag now supports personal connectors in channels
summary: Claude Tag in Slack channels now enables users to invoke personal connectors (Drive, calendar, CRM) alongside channel connectors, with audit trails preserved under each user's account. Responses can be reviewed before posting or auto-posted with sensitive content flagging.

title: Agents you can coach: how Asana builds human-agent teams with Claude
summary: Asana integrates AI agents into its Work Graph as configurable teammates with persistent memory and explicit permissions. Agent work is visible in shared tasks for colleagues to coach and refine; access is scoped by project, document, and app.

title: Projects redesigned: from folder to conversation
summary: Claude Code Projects now features multi-threaded workspaces where a coordinator orchestrates parallel work across independent threads. Added shared memory accumulates project context and decisions, with a library for files and artifacts. In beta for Claude Pro/Max subscribers using cloud sessions; Team/Enterprise rollout planned next.

title: How to prepare for AI-driven code modernization projects
summary: Anthropic's forward-deployed engineers provide a 6-step framework for organizing AI-driven code modernization in critical and regulated systems. Introduces 'certificates' (conditions every change must meet) and 'promotion policies' (review depth based on risk), with recommendations for dedicated environments, CI/CD readiness, and pilot testing.
